title.narrative: Integrated Multi-Sectoral Humanitarian Response for Conflict-Affected IDPs and Host Communities in East Borena Zone, Oromia Region.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThe proposed project, titled “Integrated Multi-Sectoral Humanitarian Response for Conflict-Affected IDPs and Host Communities in East Borena Zone, Oromia Region,” aims to deliver a coordinated, life-saving, and protection-sensitive humanitarian response addressing the urgent needs of conflict-affected populations in Wachile and Gumi Eldelo woredas of East Borena Zone, Oromia Region. Implemented by Action Against Hunger (ACF) in partnership with Community Integrated Facilitation Assistance (CIFA), the intervention aligns with the Ethiopia Humanitarian Fund (EHF) 2025 Third Reserve Allocation Strategy and contributes directly to the 2025 Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) Strategic Objectives.ltbrgtThe project will directly benefit 122,315nbspindividuals (29,617nbspwomen, 33,141nbspgirls, 27,779nbspmen, 31,778nbspboys), including 9,576 persons with disabilities. Of these, 75,563nbspare IDPs and 46,752 are host community members, with women representing 51% and children accounting for 53% of the total beneficiaries. Targeting prioritizes vulnerable groups, including children under five, pregnant and lactating women, persons with disabilities, and female-headed households, through inclusive, community-based selection and verification processes.ltbrgtThe intervention integrates five life-saving sectors: Nutrition, WASH, Protection, ES/NFI, and MPCA, to ensure a holistic and gender-responsive response.ltbrgtNutrition: 63,442 individuals (IDPs and host communities) will benefit from screening, treatment, and prevention of Severe and Moderate Acute Malnutrition (SAM/MAM) among children under five and pregnant and lactating women. Facility-based services and Mobile Health and Nutrition Teams (MHNTs) will reach remote communities, enhance Infant and Young Child Feeding in Emergencies (IYCF-E) practices, and provide capacity-building support for health workers.ltbrgtWASH: 17,788 people will benefit from water scheme rehabilitation and solarization, emergency water trucking, sanitation facility construction, and hygiene promotion, including hygiene kits and menstrual hygiene materials.ltbrgtProtection/GBV: 30,211 individuals will receive prevention and response services, including GBV case management, psychosocial support, safety audits, and community awareness sessions to promote safety and dignity.ltbrgtES/NFI: 1,768nbspdisplaced households (approximately 9,724nbspindividuals) will receive emergency shelter materials and essential non-food items, restoring safe and dignified living conditions.ltbrgtMPCA: 230 highly vulnerable households (1,150 individuals) will receive unconditional cash transfers totaling USD 46,582.18 to meet immediate food and basic needs while promoting dignity, flexibility, and local market engagement.ltbrgtThe project combines in-kind and cash-based modalities to ensure timely, flexible, and context-appropriate assistance. Localization, accountability, and community engagement are central, with transparent targeting, verification, and Complaint and Feedback Mechanisms (CFMs) ensuring inclusion and responsiveness. Coordination with Zonal and Woreda Disaster Risk Management (DRM) Offices, relevant line bureaus, and humanitarian clusters ensures complementarity and alignment with national priorities. Through this integrated and principled approach, ACF and CIFA will contribute to saving lives, restoring dignity, and strengthening resilience among 121,841 conflict-affected individuals.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtlt/pgt
